explanation_en: While 'apostar' literally means to place a bet in gambling, the construction 'apostar por' is a very common figurative expression meaning to back, support, opt for, or strongly believe in a particular course of action or solution. It is highly frequent in political, business, and personal decision-making contexts. It is always followed by the preposition 'por'.

examples.en_text: The company is betting on renewable energy for the future.
examples.target_text: La empresa apuesta por las energías renovables para el futuro.

examples.en_text: We always opt for public transportation instead of using the car.
examples.target_text: Nosotros siempre apostamos por el transporte público en lugar de usar el coche.

examples.en_text: If you want to improve your health, go for a more balanced diet.
examples.target_text: Si quieres mejorar tu salud, apuesta por una dieta más equilibrada.

examples.en_text: She opted to study graphic design and now she is very successful.
examples.target_text: Ella apostó por estudiar diseño gráfico y ahora tiene mucho éxito.

examples.en_text: It is important that the government bets on quality education.
examples.target_text: Es importante que el gobierno apueste por la educación de calidad.

examples.en_text: Supporting local businesses helps improve the neighborhood's economy.
examples.target_text: Apostar por el comercio local ayuda a mejorar la economía del barrio.

explanation_en: This prepositional phrase is used to indicate that a quantity, level, or standard is significantly higher than another reference point. The opposite is 'muy por debajo de' (well below). It is a crucial collocation for discussing statistics, expectations, or comparisons in professional and academic registers.

examples.en_text: This quarter's performance was well above our expectations.
examples.target_text: El rendimiento de este trimestre estuvo muy por encima de nuestras expectativas.

examples.en_text: The rent price in this area is well above my budget.
examples.target_text: El precio del alquiler en esta zona está muy por encima de mi presupuesto.

examples.en_text: This summer's temperatures have been well above normal.
examples.target_text: Las temperaturas de este verano han estado muy por encima de lo normal.

examples.en_text: Her English level is well above the average of her class.
examples.target_text: Su nivel de inglés está muy por encima de la media de su clase.

examples.en_text: The quality of this restaurant is well above its price.
examples.target_text: La calidad de este restaurante está muy por encima de su precio.

examples.en_text: She has work experience well above what the job requires.
examples.target_text: Ella tiene una experiencia laboral muy por encima de lo que requiere el puesto.

explanation_en: This extremely common temporal collocation is used to mark a milestone or an event that hasn't occurred for a specific duration of time. While simple in structure, it is a key building block for natural-sounding narrative and statistical reporting. Note the use of the preposition 'en' to introduce the time period, which differs from some other languages.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I saw snow for the first time in my life.
examples.target_text: Ayer vi la nieve por primera vez en mi vida.

examples.en_text: The team won the championship for the first time in ten years.
examples.target_text: El equipo ganó el campeonato por primera vez en diez años.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I turned off my phone for the first time in months.
examples.target_text: Ayer apagué mi teléfono por primera vez en meses.

examples.en_text: It rained in the desert for the first time in a decade.
examples.target_text: Llovió en el desierto por primera vez en una década.

examples.en_text: For the first time in the relationship, they spoke openly about their problems.
examples.target_text: Por primera vez en la relación, hablaron abiertamente de sus problemas.

examples.en_text: I arrived late to work for the first time in five years.
examples.target_text: Llegué tarde al trabajo por primera vez en cinco años.

explanation_en: The construction 'dar por + participle/adjective' means to consider something as being in a certain state (e.g., 'dar por sentado' - to take for granted). In this context, 'dar por rota la tregua' means to officially treat the truce as dead or terminated. It is highly common in journalistic and formal registers when discussing agreements, negotiations, or relationships.

examples.en_text: After that big argument, I decided to consider our friendship over.
examples.target_text: Después de aquella gran discusión, decidí dar por rota nuestra amistad.

examples.en_text: The director considered the negotiations broken off because they didn't reach an agreement.
examples.target_text: El director dio por rotas las negociaciones porque no llegaron a un acuerdo.

examples.en_text: If the screen doesn't turn on, we can consider the television broken.
examples.target_text: Si la pantalla no se enciende, podemos dar por rota la televisión.

examples.en_text: You cannot consider your promise broken just because things have gotten difficult.
examples.target_text: No puedes dar por rota tu promesa solo porque las cosas se han puesto difíciles.

examples.en_text: Both countries considered the alliance broken after the incident at the border.
examples.target_text: Ambos países dieron por rota la alianza tras el incidente en la frontera.

examples.en_text: Although we had problems, I don't want to consider the relationship with my brother terminated.
examples.target_text: Aunque tuvimos problemas, no quiero dar por rota la relación con mi hermano.

explanation_en: This is a strong, high-register collocation where 'irrefutable' (unquestionable/undeniable) modifies 'prueba' (proof). It is widely used in journalism, legal contexts, and formal debates to emphasize that evidence is absolute. Avoid using weaker adjectives like 'innegable' if you want to sound highly precise and authoritative.

examples.en_text: The security camera video is irrefutable proof of his innocence.
examples.target_text: El video de la cámara de seguridad es una prueba irrefutable de su inocencia.

examples.en_text: The melting of the glaciers is irrefutable proof of climate change.
examples.target_text: El derretimiento de los glaciares es una prueba irrefutable del cambio climático.

examples.en_text: She found the love letters, which was irrefutable proof of the betrayal.
examples.target_text: Encontró las cartas de amor, lo cual fue la prueba irrefutable de la traición.

examples.en_text: The increase in sales is irrefutable proof that the new strategy is working.
examples.target_text: El aumento de las ventas es una prueba irrefutable de que la nueva estrategia funciona.

examples.en_text: Archaeologists found fossils that serve as irrefutable proof of this species' existence.
examples.target_text: Los arqueólogos encontraron fósiles que sirven como prueba irrefutable de la existencia de esta especie.

examples.en_text: This email is the irrefutable proof we need to show that the client accepted the budget.
examples.target_text: Este correo electrónico es la prueba irrefutable que necesitamos para demostrar que el cliente aceptó el presupuesto.

explanation_en: The idiom 'rendir cuentas' literally means 'to render accounts' but is used metaphorically to mean 'to be held accountable' or 'to answer for one's actions'. It can be used transitively with 'a' ('rendir cuentas a alguien') to specify to whom one is accountable. It is a crucial expression in political, financial, and legal discourse.

examples.en_text: The manager has to be held accountable to the board of directors for the year's results.
examples.target_text: El gerente tiene que rendir cuentas ante la junta directiva por los resultados del año.

examples.en_text: Politicians must be held accountable to the citizens who elected them.
examples.target_text: Los políticos deben rendir cuentas a los ciudadanos que los eligieron.

examples.en_text: You are an adult now and you don't have to answer to anyone about what you do.
examples.target_text: Ya eres un adulto y no tienes que rendirle cuentas a nadie sobre lo que haces.

examples.en_text: At the end of the project, we will have to account for all the expenses incurred.
examples.target_text: Al final del proyecto, tendremos que rendir cuentas de todos los gastos realizados.

examples.en_text: Sooner or later, the guilty party will have to answer to justice.
examples.target_text: Tarde o temprano, el culpable tendrá que rendir cuentas ante la justicia.

examples.en_text: I don't like my partner asking me to account for every minute of my day.
examples.target_text: No me gusta que mi pareja me pida rendir cuentas de cada minuto de mi día.

explanation_en: This rhetorical construction uses 'hasta dónde' (how far / to what limit) combined with the future tense of 'llegar' (to arrive/reach) to question the limits of an abstract concept like patience, tolerance, or power. It is a very natural way to frame analytical questions in journalism and essays. Note that 'llegar' is used here instead of 'ir' (to go) to emphasize reaching a critical threshold.

examples.en_text: I wonder how far artificial intelligence will go in the coming years.
examples.target_text: Me pregunto hasta dónde llegará la inteligencia artificial en los próximos años.

examples.en_text: With such a positive attitude, I don't know how far he will go in his professional career.
examples.target_text: Con esa actitud tan positiva, no sé hasta dónde llegará en su carrera profesional.

examples.en_text: This argument is getting out of hand; how far will this conflict go?
examples.target_text: Esta discusión se está saliendo de control; ¿hasta dónde llegará este conflicto?

examples.en_text: Prices keep rising and people are wondering how far inflation will go.
examples.target_text: Los precios siguen subiendo y la gente se pregunta hasta dónde llegará la inflación.

examples.en_text: With so many lies, I don't know how far they will go to get what they want.
examples.target_text: Con tantas mentiras, no sé hasta dónde llegarán para conseguir lo que quieren.

examples.en_text: Excuse me, how far will this train go? Does it end its route in Madrid?
examples.target_text: Disculpe, ¿hasta dónde llegará este tren? ¿Termina su recorrido en Madrid?

explanation_en: Derived from card games, 'jugar varias cartas' (or 'jugar sus cartas') means to pursue multiple strategies or keep several options open simultaneously. It is a common metaphorical expression in political analysis and business strategy. It highlights a pragmatic, multi-faceted approach to a complex problem.

examples.en_text: To find a job quickly, he decided to play several cards: he sent his resume to various companies and contacted former colleagues.
examples.target_text: Para encontrar trabajo pronto, decidió jugar varias cartas: mandó su currículum a varias empresas y contactó a antiguos compañeros.

examples.en_text: We cannot depend on a single client; in this negotiation, we have to play several cards to ensure success.
examples.target_text: No podemos depender de un solo cliente; en esta negociación tenemos que jugar varias cartas para asegurar el éxito.

examples.en_text: During the last round of the game, she played several cards in a row and managed to win the match.
examples.target_text: Durante la última ronda del juego, ella jugó varias cartas seguidas y logró ganar la partida.

examples.en_text: The government is playing several cards at the same time to try to stop the economic crisis.
examples.target_text: El gobierno está jugando varias cartas a la vez para intentar frenar la crisis económica.

examples.en_text: Since I wasn't sure which major to choose, I played several cards and submitted my application to three different universities.
examples.target_text: Como no estaba seguro de qué carrera elegir, jugué varias cartas y presenté mi solicitud en tres universidades distintas.

examples.en_text: The company is going to play several cards in its new marketing campaign to attract all types of audiences.
examples.target_text: La empresa va a jugar varias cartas en su nueva campaña de marketing para atraer a todo tipo de público.

explanation_en: The passive-like construction 'verse + adjective/participle' describes how someone perceives their situation or finds themselves. 'Constreñido' (constrained/restricted) is a sophisticated C1-level vocabulary word. This combination is highly elegant and preferred in formal analysis over simpler alternatives like 'estar limitado por'.

examples.en_text: The director found himself constrained by the project's limited budget.
examples.target_text: El director se vio constreñido por el presupuesto limitado del proyecto.

examples.en_text: Many families find themselves constrained by the lack of free time in their daily lives.
examples.target_text: Muchas familias se ven constreñidas por la falta de tiempo libre en su día a día.

examples.en_text: She felt constrained by the company's strict rules and decided to resign.
examples.target_text: Ella se vio constreñida por las estrictas normas de la empresa y decidió renunciar.

examples.en_text: If we don't organize the work now, we will find ourselves constrained by the deadlines.
examples.target_text: Si no organizamos el trabajo ahora, nos veremos constreñidos por los plazos de entrega.

examples.en_text: The young artist did not want to be constrained by the public's expectations.
examples.target_text: El joven artista no quería verse constreñido por las expectativas del público.

examples.en_text: The scientists found themselves constrained by the lack of resources to continue the study.
examples.target_text: Los científicos se vieron constreñidos por la falta de recursos para continuar el estudio.

explanation_en: The idiom 'no temblarle el pulso (a alguien)' literally means 'one's pulse/hand does not shake' and is used to describe someone who acts with absolute determination, ruthlessness, or without hesitation. It is often used in political and military contexts to depict leaders who are willing to make tough or extreme decisions. It is always used with indirect object pronouns (e.g., 'no le tiembla el pulso').

examples.en_text: The director didn't hesitate when he had to fire the employees who weren't working.
examples.target_text: Al director no le tembló el pulso cuando tuvo que despedir a los empleados que no trabajaban.

examples.en_text: If you keep treating me with disrespect, I won't hesitate to end our relationship.
examples.target_text: Si sigues tratándome con falta de respeto, no me va a temblar el pulso para cortar nuestra relación.

examples.en_text: The police do not hesitate when it comes to enforcing the law against criminals.
examples.target_text: A la policía no le tiembla el pulso a la hora de aplicar la ley contra los delincuentes.

examples.en_text: The surgeon is very confident; he doesn't waver in life-or-death situations.
examples.target_text: El cirujano es muy seguro de sí mismo; no le tiembla el pulso en las situaciones de vida o muerte.

examples.en_text: In times of crisis, bad leaders hesitate to make difficult decisions.
examples.target_text: En los momentos de crisis, a los malos líderes les tiembla el pulso para tomar decisiones difíciles.

examples.en_text: My parents didn't hesitate to punish us if we did something dangerous.
examples.target_text: A mis padres no les temblaba el pulso para castigarnos si hacíamos algo peligroso.

explanation_en: While 'fondo de armario' literally refers to 'wardrobe essentials' in fashion, it is used metaphorically in Spain to describe a deep reserve, backlog, or stockpile of resources (like players on a sports team or, in this case, military ammunition). It implies having a reliable, deep pool of assets to draw from. This is a highly idiomatic, native-level usage that will impress examiners and native speakers alike.

examples.en_text: A good white shirt is an essential garment for any basic wardrobe.
examples.target_text: Una buena camisa blanca es una prenda imprescindible para cualquier fondo de armario.

examples.en_text: The team won the tournament because they have excellent squad depth with very good substitutes.
examples.target_text: El equipo ganó el torneo porque tiene un excelente fondo de armario con muy buenos suplentes.

examples.en_text: In our company, we always have a good reserve of professionals for new projects.
examples.target_text: En nuestra empresa siempre tenemos un buen fondo de armario de profesionales para los nuevos proyectos.

examples.en_text: Before buying trendy clothes, you should invest in a good basic wardrobe.
examples.target_text: Antes de comprar ropa de moda, deberías invertir en un buen fondo de armario.

examples.en_text: With so many injured players, the coach had to resort to the squad depth.
examples.target_text: Con tantos jugadores lesionados, el entrenador tuvo que recurrir al fondo de armario.

examples.en_text: We need a good reserve of ideas in case this plan doesn't work.
examples.target_text: Necesitamos un buen fondo de armario de ideas por si este plan no funciona.

explanation_en: This is an extremely common colloquial filler and idiomatic phrase meaning 'so to speak' or 'as they say'. It is used to soften a statement, metaphor, or exaggeration, making it sound more natural in spoken Spanish. It is grammatically fixed and does not change regardless of who is speaking.

examples.en_text: We have already finished the project, so to speak; only the director's signature is missing.
examples.target_text: Ya hemos terminado el proyecto, como quien dice; solo falta la firma del director.

examples.en_text: I live right next door, so to speak, just two minutes from your house.
examples.target_text: Vivo aquí al lado, como quien dice, a solo dos minutos de tu casa.

examples.en_text: She is, so to speak, the head of the family, even if she doesn't admit it.
examples.target_text: Ella es, como quien dice, la jefa de la familia, aunque no lo admita.

examples.en_text: The trip is already paid for, so to speak, because we booked it months ago.
examples.target_text: El viaje ya está pagado, como quien dice, porque lo reservamos hace meses.

examples.en_text: I've just started learning piano, so to speak; I've only been at it for two weeks.
examples.target_text: Acabo de empezar a aprender piano, como quien dice; solo llevo dos semanas.

examples.en_text: With this discount, the coat is practically free, so to speak.
examples.target_text: Con este descuento, el abrigo nos sale gratis, como quien dice.
